venue.name: CFB Esquimalt Naval and Military Museum
venue.description: The CFB Esquimalt Naval & Military Museum is located at Naden on Canadian Forces Base Esquimalt in Esquimalt, BC, and collects, preserves, interprets and displays the history of the naval presence on Canada's West Coast and of the military on southern Vancouver Island. Its exhibits focus on Canada's Navy on the West Coast, the Canadian Women's Army Corps, the Women's Royal Canadian Naval Service and the West Coast Defences, and it includes the Oriole Children's Gallery, an archive and library, and guided and self-guided tours.
venue.hours_notes: The site gives two different sets of hours. The Visitors page body (modified 2026-08-11) says "Open 10:00am - 3:30pm, 7 days a week!" and "We are always closed on Statutory Holidays." The sidebar that appears on every page says May 1 - Sep 2: 7 days a week 10:00am - 3:30pm, and Sep 3 - Apr 30: Monday to Friday 10:00am - 3:30pm. The Archives and Office are open Monday to Friday 8:00am - 4:00pm year round. The site asks visitors to call (250) 363-5655 or (250) 363-4312 to confirm the museum is open.
venue.seasonal_notes: Guided tours for school groups are free of charge in November as part of the museum's Remembrance Day programming. The museum is inside CFB Esquimalt: entrance to the base is off Admirals Rd and Woodway Rd, and those aged 18+ may need to show government photo ID to enter the base. From the Naden main gate it is about a 10 minute walk to the museum.

programs.name: Self-guided museum visit
programs.description: The museum is open to the general public and coordinates self-guided as well as guided tours of its exhibits and displays. Admission is by suggested cash donation: Adults $10, Seniors/Students $5, Families $25. The Oriole Children's Gallery is described as "a classroom in a museum" and offers imaginative activities for youngsters between 4-8 years, including dress-up play uniforms, an introduction to naval terms, diver gear and life jackets, games and a magnet board, signal flags and activities, and nautical-themed children's books. Access to the museum requires entering CFB Esquimalt; visitors aged 18+ may need to show government photo ID at the gate.
programs.evidence: Admission is by suggested cash donation.

programs.name: Guided group tour
programs.description: The museum coordinates guided tours of its exhibits and displays and welcomes tour requests from visiting groups; museum staff will work with the group to tailor a tour that suits its needs. The standard fee is $75 per guided tour, with a discounted $50 fee for tours for seniors. The museum states it can negotiate reduced fees for tours, or waive fees entirely, for groups and organizations with limited funds. The $75 is stated as a tour fee, not a per-person fee; the page does not say whether admission donations are additional. Tour duration, maximum group size and lead time are not stated. The Tours page was last modified 2024-07-05.
programs.evidence: There is a $75 standard fee for guided tours, and a discounted fee of $50 for tours for seniors.

programs.name: School visit & tour
programs.description: The museum offers school visits and tours and states it can work with the teacher's curriculum. Teachers are encouraged to view the museum's listing on the BC Field Trips site and to contact the museum to arrange a tour. Free downloadable teacher resources are offered: a tri-fold Kids Quiz combining text and images for elementary and middle school age classes, and a more advanced General Quiz for older students covering general knowledge questions; both are PDF, English only. No price, group size limit, duration, grade range or booking lead time is published for school visits outside the free November tours.
programs.evidence: We can work with your curriculum to provide students with a relevant and thought-provoking learning experience.

programs.name: Free November school group guided tour (Remembrance Day programming)
programs.description: In November only, guided tours for school groups are offered free of charge as part of the museum's Remembrance Day programming. No group size limit, duration, grade range or booking lead time is stated.
programs.evidence: Guided tours for school groups are offered free of charge in November, as part of our Remembrance Day programming.

gaps: Child admission is not stated. The suggested donation list is Adults $10, Seniors/Students $5, Families $25 - there is no separate child or preschooler line, and no minimum age.
Whether the $75 guided tour fee applies to school groups outside November, and whether admission donations are charged on top of the tour fee, is not stated.
Tour duration and maximum group size are never stated anywhere on the site.
Booking lead time is not stated. The only booking route given for schools is a "Book Visit" button pointing to the Contact page.

Hours conflict: the Visitors page body (modified 2026-08-11) says open 7 days a week and always closed on statutory holidays, while the site-wide sidebar says 7 days a week only May 1 - Sep 2 and Monday to Friday Sep 3 - Apr 30. Confirm by phone.

The Contact page (last modified 2024-03-28) still carries an un-removed COVID-19 notice saying "we are temporarily closed" and that archives are available Thursdays and Fridays only. This contradicts the Visitors page and appears to be stale. The contact form on that page requires JavaScript and did not render.
Washrooms, lunch or picnic space for a class, and rain backup are not mentioned anywhere on the site.
Wheelchair and stroller accessibility are not mentioned anywhere on the site.

Parking is not described at all, and there is no mention of bus or coach parking or a drop-off point. The directions PDF only covers arrival by car and by BC Transit (routes 15, 24, 25, 26, then about a 10 minute walk from the Naden main gate).

Base access is a real constraint for a school trip: the museum is inside CFB Esquimalt and those aged 18+ may need to show government photo ID to enter. Whether a bus of children plus chaperones needs advance clearance is not stated.

Two different email addresses are published: Info@NavalAndMilitaryMuseum.org in the site footer and tatiana.robinson@forces.gc.ca on the Tours page for service enquiries. The Tours page address was recorded because it is the one given for arranging services.
The museum's detailed school programming is described on a third-party site (bcfieldtrips.ca) that was not used as a source.
